Confusable pairs among weather and rural driving rules, where similar-sounding emergencies call for different responses; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec08-R01 | anchor: A01
When hydroplaning you neither brake nor turn until the tires grip the road again; you only ease off the gas and hold the wheel straight. [A01]
Why it matters: group loss of traction; confusable hydroplaning versus skidding (skid steering is on the next page).
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R02 | anchor: A01
Gently pumping the brakes is the advice for cars without ABS, while the general slick-road advice for every car is to avoid rapid braking. [A01]
Why it matters: group braking; confusable ABS versus non-ABS.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R03 | anchor: A01
In poor visibility, a vehicle that looks slow may actually be moving faster than it appears. [A01]
Why it matters: group visibility; misconception what you see is the true speed.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R04 | anchor: A01
Ice forms first on bridges and overpasses and in shady spots, so these can be slippery even while the open road is not. [A01]
Why it matters: group ice; misconception the whole road freezes at once.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R05 | anchor: A01
The first minutes of rain are a slippery time, not a safe one, because the handbook lists pavement just as it starts to rain among likely slick spots. [A01]
Why it matters: group rain; misconception light rain is harmless.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R06 | anchor: A01
Bald tires do two separate kinds of harm: they reduce traction and they make stopping distances longer. [A01]
Why it matters: group tires; prereq traction.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R07 | anchor: A02
In a skid you stay off the brake, steer where you want to go, and then steer back the other way as the car straightens. [A02]
Why it matters: group skids; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-R08 | anchor: A02
Winter driving calls for headlights on but high beams off, while the snowplow rule is about distance: at least 200 feet behind a plow with flashing lights. [A02]
Why it matters: group winter; confusable headlights versus following distance.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-R09 | anchor: A02
The snowplow distance applies whether the plow's flashing lights are red, amber or green. [A02]
Why it matters: group winter; misconception only amber lights count.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-R10 | anchor: A02
Clearing snow and ice covers the lamps, side mirrors and license plates as well as every window. [A02]
Why it matters: group winter; misconception only the windshield needs clearing.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-R11 | anchor: A02
Livestock on or along the highway get the right-of-way, and you slow down and keep a safe distance rather than using the horn. [A02]
Why it matters: group rural; confusable livestock versus farm machinery.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-R12 | anchor: A02
Farm machinery may lack brake lights and turn signals, so you cannot count on it signaling a stop or turn. [A02]
Why it matters: group rural; misconception farm vehicles always signal.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]
